# The distributions7 package {#sec-distributions7}

Where @sec-links dealt with a transformation of a single number, this chapter
deals with the object that transformation serves: a parametric family of
probability distributions, carrying not only its density but everything a
modelling routine might want to know about it.

The chapter is long because the package is, and it divides into four parts that
can be read in order or dipped into. @sec-distributions sets out what a
`distrib` object is obliged to provide and develops the likelihood theory the
package rests on — score, observed and expected information, the Bartlett
identities in full generality, derivatives transported onto the unconstrained
scale by Faà di Bruno's formula, derivatives with respect to the response, and
derivatives of the distribution function that make censored likelihoods
possible — before presenting the fourteen families themselves.

@sec-transformations turns to **operators on distributions**: a change of
variables, zero-inflation, zero-adjustment and truncation, each of which takes a
distribution and returns another one with all of the same machinery intact. The
mathematics there is more interesting than it may sound, because the derivatives
of the constructed model must be assembled from those of its parent, and doing
that at fourth order in general requires a small amount of combinatorics.

@sec-fitting puts the apparatus to work on the simplest problem that exercises
all of it, maximum likelihood for an i.i.d. sample, and @sec-fallbacks describes
what a distribution receives when it implements nothing but its density — the
part of the package that decides whether a family the author never anticipated
is a first-class citizen or a second-class one.
